kit.name: Library robot voice
kit.why: The parent picked it: a real robot voice for the droid. Moved to Eleven v4 with an audio tag on every line (tools/audio/direction.json): the parent approved tagged v4 after auditions, 12 October.

knight.name: Library knight voice (v4)
knight.why: The parent picked it after an audition: a heroic, earnest young knight. Eleven v4 at ElevenLabs' character-voice setting (v4 takes only stability and similarity), with an audio tag in front of every line (tools/audio/direction.json). Without a tag, a line falls flat.

gunner.name: Jessica
gunner.why: Bright, playful, energetic young American female, for a cocky, fast-talking sky-pirate. Moved to Eleven v4 with an audio tag on every line (tools/audio/direction.json): the parent approved tagged v4 after auditions, 12 October.

spellwright.name: Library wizard voice
spellwright.why: The parent picked it: the wizard. Moved to Eleven v4 with an audio tag on every line (tools/audio/direction.json): the parent approved tagged v4 after auditions, 12 October.

titancaller.name: Lily
titancaller.why: Warm, velvety British actress: calm and poetic, and grand when she summons. Moved to Eleven v4 with an audio tag on every line (tools/audio/direction.json): the parent approved tagged v4 after auditions, 12 October.

trailer.name: Brian
trailer.why: Deep, resonant American male for the booming movie-trailer narration of his Titan entrances. He reads the boy's own summon words live, so they can't be pre-recorded; on eleven_multilingual_v2 he couldn't take a tag and read them flat. Moved to Eleven v4 with a live tag ([booming epic movie-trailer announcer, slow and dramatic], LIVE_TAGS in src/ai/providers.js) after the parent said the voice for Tidebreaker rising sounded flat, 17 October.

spelling.name: Matilda
spelling.why: Clear, friendly American female with careful diction, for reading spelling words.

narrator.name: George
narrator.why: Warm British storyteller, for adventure narration. Moved to Eleven v4 with an audio tag on every line (tools/audio/direction.json): the parent approved tagged v4 after auditions, 12 October. On 17 October the parent said every narrator line sounded very flat: at stability 0.5 with one bland tag in front of a long line he read evenly, so his stability came down to 0.3 like the characters and each line became a whole performance, a lively storyteller tag up front and a tag at each turn.

jumble.name: Library pirate voice
jumble.why: The parent picked it for Captain Jumble, the loud, vain, theatrical ghost-pirate. On Eleven v4 with one tag per line he sounded like an American man, not a pirate, so every line is now a whole performance (tools/audio/direction.json): a tag describing a gravelly, sinister pirate, then a tag at each turn, after the parent's own test of his ending line, 12 October. That test set stability and similarity low, without numbers. v4 takes both as plain numbers, and no v4 preset (like v3's Creative) was found to match, so low here is 0.15 stability, for a freer, more theatrical read, and 0.35 similarity, so the pirate tag can pull him away from the voice's plain read.

beastkeeper.name: Tamsin's voice
beastkeeper.why: The parent cast it for Tamsin, the Beastkeeper (chapter 2): a girl of about twelve, flat and exact, kinder to fiends than to people. Eleven v4 at the characters' setting, with a tag on every line (tools/audio/direction.json). The parent approved test clips of it, 13 October.

clamp.name: Inspector Clamp's voice
clamp.why: The parent cast it for Inspector Clamp, chapter 2's villain: polite, cold and bureaucratic. It also speaks the Drain Engine's barks from its cockpit (ENGINE_BARKS in src/content/barks.js). Eleven v4 at the characters' setting, with a tag on every line. The parent approved test clips of it, 13 October.

keeper.why: The parent cast it for the old lighthouse keeper (chapter 2): an old man who has forgotten nearly everything but his climb to the lamp. Eleven v4 at the characters' setting, with a tag on every line. The parent approved test clips of it, 13 October.

hal.why: The parent cast it for Honest Hal, the harbor's shopkeeper (chapter 2): jovial and smooth, with sums that only go wrong one way. Eleven v4 at the characters' setting, with a tag on every line. The parent approved test clips of it, 13 October.

swordmaster.name: The Sword Master's voice
swordmaster.why: The parent cast it for the Sword Master (chapter 2): grand and theatrical, and stuck for a comeback. Eleven v4 at the characters' setting, with a tag on every line. The parent approved test clips of it, 13 October.
